elements.el: Tables sit in a flush card
Tables scroll inside their own box
Tables become stacked rows on a phone
elements.reason: the kit's stacked table, the audit log's too; the RunsPhone ledger says how a run's row stacks

bundle.css keeps an id cell on one line; on a desktop the runs page draws a job id as a box of its own, as wide as the id and at most 22 characters of the code face (runs-css.mjs RUNS_TABLE.idMaxCh), inside which a longer id breaks, at a hyphen first, since one scheduler's repeat:<trigger>:<slot> made the Job column 282 px wide for every row; 22 and not the card's 12, which broke a forge delivery's id (gh- and a GUID, 39 to 42 characters) into four or five lines where 22 hold it in two; on a phone it moves to the next line whole (the RunsPhone ledger)

elements.el: The outcome cell is a badge plus its reason sentence
elements.reason: a completed run draws the badge alone, in the idle tone with the ok glyph, and so does a run whose outcome word says why (awaiting input, cancelled), as the RunsScreen card draws them

elements.el: Every run row carries its project tag
elements.reason: the record's project, in the target's cell; a record with none has no tag

elements.el: wide cells span the full row, and each cell has a data-l label for the phone layout
elements.reason: bundle.css spans a wide cell across a stacked row and draws a cell's data-l before it; the runs table labels only the host and the cost, as the RunsPhone card does, since the kit writes no data-l for a column whose phone label is "", so the outcome cell spans the row unlabelled

elements.el: The foot: how many rows, then Newer and Older
elements.reason: Newer quiet and Older the plain button, each disabled where there is no page; the runs page names its Newer Newest (the RunsScreen ledger)

elements.el: Sample rows: gh-e9a0, gh-a91e, gh-2f6a, gh-f0c2 and gh-ebd7, "5 of 27 runs"
elements.reason: sample rows and their sentences; the goldens draw the fixture deployment's records
